title: Adaptive fairness layer and graceful burst fallbacks for dedicated clusters
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a recent dedicated-cluster capacity incident we observed multi-tenant saturation driven by a single tenant with spiky token throughput and large KV-cache churn. This ticket implements an "adaptive fairness layer" (runtime gating + graded throttling) plus a short-term reservation-rightsizing procedure and a hardened burst fallback so noisy workloads do not cascade into eviction storms.
impact_summary: Incident produced elevated tail-latency for premium tenants and two small-scale eviction waves across 3 pools. Customer-visible errors spiked for 1 hour and billing anomalies for affected tenants were reported. Root causes: inadequate soft-reservation hysteresis, a permissive burst token policy, and missing early noisy-tenant detection signals.

investigation_findings: Noisy tenant behavior: single tenant produced 7x normal prefix variance and large KV cache invalidations which prevented effective KV reuse
Soft-reservation hysteresis was too short: reservations decayed aggressively on brief inactivity, enabling a subsequent burst to consume free capacity
Burst token bucket allowed large instant bursts tuned for average cases; combined with reservation decay this caused sustained oversubscription
Detection gaps: current noisy-neighbor detector uses 5-minute sliding windows which delayed mitigation; need sub-minute heuristics for hot-start bursts
Telemetry surfaced: host_gpu_utilization spiked to 98% and host_eviction_rate increased 12x during the incident (panels: https://dash.redwood.example/evictions?range=6h)
Existing runbook steps were followed but lacked an automated fallback path; manual intervention took ~25 minutes to bring stable state
proposed_actions: 1) Build 'adaptive fairness layer' in the serving runtime: per-tenant micro-queues that enforce graded throttling based on short-window burst score and reservation headroom
2) Implement short-window noisy-signal detector (30s) using KV-hit-rate, prefix-growth, and instant token rate; trigger automated soft-fence (temporary token shed) when threshold crossed
3) Adjust reservation decay to include hysteresis: reservations should not shrink more than 10% within a 10-minute window without operator approval
4) Rework burst-token policy: introduce decaying burst budget tied to recent sustained usage rather than instantaneous peaks (token half-life = 90s default)
5) Reservation-rightsizing playbook: an automated suggestion engine that recommends reservation increases for tenants that exceed sustained throughput for 15m and an operator-facing approval flow
6) Add eviction-dampening in allocator: when eviction rate is rising, temporarily tighten burst budgets cluster-wide and bias scheduling to pinned reservations
7) Create a canary rollout plan and load-test scenario simulating KV churn patterns and prefix churn (use qps-replay tool) before enabling adaptive fairness in production
8) Update runbook with automated mitigation steps and a fast rollback flag; add a dashboard panel for 'short-window burst score' and alerting
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive fairness layer implemented and feature-flagged in runtime-1.21
Short-window noisy detector emits events within 30s and triggers automatic soft-fence in staging tests
Reservation decay hysteresis added and validated in controlled load tests (no reservation reduction >10% within 10m under test)
Burst token decay behavior validated with synthetic workload: observed max sustained oversubscription reduced by >=60% in test cluster
New dashboard panels and alerts live: short-window-burst-score, per-tenant-kv-hit-rate, eviction-dampening-state
Runbook updated and tabletop drill executed with SRE + support; mean time to automated mitigation under 3 minutes in drills
